title: The eighth watcher
topic: In Friendswood and League City, the Galveston County Consolidated Drainage District switched on seven radar flood sensors whose readings AI tools combine with rain, gauge, weather and soil data to help predict how floods could develop, on a colour-coded public map with text alerts.
hook: Why is everyone staring at this creek?

treatment.logline: A Friendswood street that still walks out every morning to stare at Clear Creek since Harvey gets a new regular on the bridge rail, a radar sensor that stares along with them, and the choice to stay or go stays theirs.
treatment.cold_open: Neighbours in robes with coffee mugs line the Clear Creek bank like a gallery crowd while one woman settles into her lawn chair. Before second three the camera finds a small sensor on the bridge rail tilting its head at the same angle as the people, then blinking.
treatment.turn: Seven lights sit along more than 80 miles of creeks, ditches and bayous, and ghost rings mark where the district says it still needs gauges. The map decides nothing. The resident stands at her door with her keys and decides for herself.
treatment.button: Next dawn the chair is back at the creek with a green map on the phone on its armrest. The neighbours still walk out, and the sensor blinks back at them. Now the creek can answer.

scenes.vo: In Friendswood, people come outside and look at the creek every day.

draw.subject: neighbours in robes with coffee mugs
draw.action: shuffle onto the bank and line up staring at the water while the resident sets her lawn chair down, coffee mug on the armrest
draw.emotion: the resident squints at the creek, wary

draw.subject: the sensor on the bridge rail
draw.action: tilts its head to the same angle as the people below and blinks

scenes.vo: Jason Jones, who sits on the local drainage board, says it is almost like PTSD from Harvey and other rain events.

draw.subject: Jones
draw.action: walks up to the bridge rail and looks down at the creek

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: presses a hand to her chest as a grey storm memory named Harvey and Allison rolls over her porch

scenes.vo: That fear has a ranking. The board's president, Rusty Burkett, calls flooding and drainage the number one threat to lives and property in Galveston County.

draw.subject: a quote card
draw.action: slides up beside the board president as he nods

draw.subject: the quote's words
draw.action: underline themselves one line at a time as Burkett points at the card

draw.subject: a big number one
draw.action: slams onto the card and the card shakes

scenes.vo: Yet until this spring, Jones says, the county had no flood sensors at all.

draw.subject: the county map
draw.action: sits dark with its creek lines unlit while a cricket chirps

draw.subject: Jones
draw.action: shrugs beside the dark map

scenes.vo: So in April, the Galveston County Consolidated Drainage District switched on seven radar sensors, six in the Clear Creek watershed and one in the Dickinson Bayou watershed. Each cost less than ten thousand dollars.

draw.subject: seven sensors along the creek
draw.action: open their eyes one after another, receding downstream from the bridge

draw.subject: a calendar page
draw.action: flips to April above the creek as the first sensor wakes

draw.subject: six sensors
draw.action: blink green along Clear Creek while a lone seventh on Dickinson Bayou waves its light

draw.subject: a district crew member
draw.action: bolts the sensor onto the rail and hangs a price tag on it, and the sensor opens its eyes

scenes.vo: One reading is one spot on one creek. So the system adds rainfall totals, stream gauges, weather stations and how soaked the soil already is.

draw.subject: the sensor
draw.action: fires a radar pulse down to the water and catches the echo as the crew member looks up
draw.emotion: the crew member squints up, impressed

draw.subject: a single dot
draw.action: blinks alone on a long creek line

draw.subject: four pipes
draw.action: fill one by one and pour rain, gauge, weather and soil into the glass box with the sensor

draw.subject: a soil sponge
draw.action: is already dripping, so a raindrop runs straight off it

scenes.vo: Then AI tools help predict how a flood could develop, even how conditions upstream could affect neighborhoods downstream.

draw.subject: dotted could-paths
draw.action: spread across the resident's phone at her kitchen table

draw.subject: a low swell
draw.action: rolls down the creek past the near-bank houses, staying in its banks

scenes.vo: Residents see it as a map. Green means safe. Yellow, flooding possible. Red, flooding likely.

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: steps onto her porch past the glider and lifts her phone

draw.subject: the green light
draw.action: pops on in the legend

draw.subject: the yellow light
draw.action: pops on beside it

draw.subject: the red light
draw.action: pops on and pulses once

scenes.vo: They can sign up for alerts on one creek, and the platform is set to text them when the water rises to a level officials set.

draw.subject: the resident's thumb
draw.action: taps the Clear Creek point and a bell icon lights

draw.subject: a district crew member
draw.action: drags the alert slider on a laptop to a line

draw.subject: the rain
draw.action: sweeps over the empty lawn chair as the creek climbs and the phone buzzes

scenes.vo: The map does not decide anything. Jones says it helps people choose whether a road is still passable, or whether it is time to leave.

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: stands at her door with the folded chair and lifts her keys

draw.subject: a route line on her phone
draw.action: draws around the low street toward high ground

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: closes her hand on the keys

scenes.vo: Seven sensors are a start. The district maintains more than 80 miles of creeks, ditches and bayous, and executive director Paige Bailey says the system has already mapped where it needs more gauges.

draw.subject: the camera
draw.action: pulls back along a long ribbon of creeks and ditches until the seven lights are tiny and the lone one looks very alone

draw.subject: the ditches and side creeks
draw.action: draw themselves on branch by branch while a pulse runs down the main creek

draw.subject: Bailey
draw.action: walks the dark bank and plants a dashed ghost stake

draw.subject: dashed ghost rings
draw.action: pop up along the map where more gauges are needed as Bailey points at them

scenes.vo: For now, it covers only Friendswood and League City. People still walk out to look at the creek. Now the creek can answer back.

draw.subject: two town pins
draw.action: glow on the map while the rest of the county stays grey

draw.subject: the resident
draw.action: sets the chair back on the bank and lays her green phone on the armrest

draw.subject: the sensor
draw.action: blinks green and waves back at the neighbours over the lawn chair with its green phone
